subject: VelocityPay — urgent throughput collapse and elevated 5xx/latency
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@velocitypay.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Li <marco.li@velocitypay.com>
Date: 2027-11-13T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: High 5xx & latency impacting checkouts — urgent

Hi Sofia,

We started seeing a sharp drop in throughput and a wave of 5xx + long tail latencies on our Reserved capacity around 07:45 PST. Checkout conversions are down ~22% and internal ops are getting paged.

Attached are a short QPS trace and a small sample of gateway logs highlighting elevated error_ratio and long sequence lengths. Key details: our reserved commit is 1.2M tokens/hr; observed token ingress is within expected range but token processing is much slower and many requests time out at our client deadline.

Can Redwood start an emergency investigation and provide a workaround (fallback model, routing change, or burst allocation)? We need an ETA — this is impacting revenue.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Reliability — VelocityPay

Attachments: qps-trace.csv, prod-sample-logs.json
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@velocitypay.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-13T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx & latency impacting checkouts — urgent

Hi Elena — thank you for the data and the heads up. Sorry you're seeing this — we are on it.

Immediate actions:
- I've alerted engineering and ops (cc'd).
- We will open a 30-min bridge now to triage and confirm scope (invite attached).
- Short-term: we'll test a routing fallback to the compatible "xlarge-legacy-quant" variant and enable stricter per-request batching caps.
- If needed, we'll request temporary burst GPUs from our Dedicated pool for 2 hours to restore throughput while we diagnose root cause.

Please join the bridge if possible; if not, we will update every 15 minutes. We will also capture a customer-facing timeline and next steps.

Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147

Attachment: bridge-invite.ics
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-13T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: FW: VelocityPay urgent — initial telemetry attached (internal)

Jonas, Rishi — forwarding VelocityPay's report and qps/log samples. TL;DR: reserved commit appears intact but effective throughput is collapsing with elevated 5xx and long P95/P99 latencies starting ~07:45 PST. Customer impact: checkout failures.

First-pass telemetry from our side:
- Spike in KV cache miss rate for this tenant (orders include many long prefixes).
- Several long-sequence requests (token lengths > 2.5x baseline) causing model hot paths to be occupied longer than usual.
- A subset of requests are being routed to the new xlarge-qa-v2 variant (~auto-rollout last week) which has higher per-token latency under long sequences on current kernels.

Immediate asks:
1) Can we force fallback routing for VelocityPay to xlarge-legacy-quant or a lower-latency variant?
2) Can we authorize a burst of GPUs from the shared Dedicated pool (8 GPUs, 2 hours) while we mitigate? Ops will need approval from Priyom for billing/credits.
3) Any quick kernel/parameter tweaks we can apply to reduce P99?

Customer is on a bridge in ~10m. I will be on the call.

— Sofia
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-13T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: VelocityPay urgent — initial telemetry attached (internal)

Thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. Quick note from the runtime side after a fast triage:

Root cause hypothesis (fast):
- The auto-rollout of xlarge-qa-v2 last week introduced a kernel path that degrades under long-sequence workloads on our current Xavier kernels. Under mixed tenant load, the variant holds GPU contexts longer and increases scheduler jitter.
- KV cache pressure is amplifying tail latency because cold-starts for long prefixes are expensive.

Mitigations we can execute in the next 15–30m:
1) Force route VelocityPay off xlarge-qa-v2 to xlarge-legacy-quant (compatible API surface, lower P95). This is fast (config change).
2) Turn on aggressive prefix/KV caching for VelocityPay only — we can seed popular prefixes from recent logs. This reduces cold starts.
3) Apply a soft per-request token cap (e.g., max_tokens=512) at the routing layer for this tenant to lower tail pressure while preserving most requests.

If the above don't bring latency down to acceptable levels, we should request an emergency dedicated burst (8 x A100-style GPUs) for 2 hours to clear the backlog while we roll back the variant. Ops will need Priyom to approve excess capacity and any credits.

I'll start the routing change now and report back with telemetry in 10m.

— Jonas (runtime team)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-13T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: VelocityPay emergency — proposed remediation and ask for approval (internal)

Quick plan and asks for leadership approval: 

Immediate remediation (operational):
- Execute Jonas' routing override to xlarge-legacy-quant (in flight).
- Enable tenant-only aggressive KV pre-seeding and set per-request max_tokens=512.
- Deploy a temporary rate-shaping policy: burst window = 30s, token cap per-window to avoid queueing storms.

Emergency capacity ask: request allocation of 8 GPUs from the Dedicated burst pool for 2 hours (priority: high). Expected outcomes: clears queued requests, reduces client timeouts while we complete variant rollback and kernel patching. Estimated overage: will trigger billing reconciliation and potential SLA credits; ask Priyom to approve.

Customer comms: propose we tell VelocityPay a 2-hour mitigation window with updates every 15–20 minutes and a commitment to a postmortem + SLA credit assessment.

Priyom — can you approve the burst allocation and any emergency credit we need to offer? If yes, ops will authorize and we will start right away.

— Rishi
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@velocitypay.com>, Marco Li <marco.li@velocitypay.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-13T17:42:00-08:00
Subject: VelocityPay incident — immediate fixes deployed and next steps

Elena / Marco — thank you again for the quick escalation and patience today. Below is a concise summary of what we did and the immediate plan: 

What we executed (completed):
- Forced routing override for VelocityPay from xlarge-qa-v2 -> xlarge-legacy-quant (completed at 10:12 PST).
- Enabled tenant-scoped aggressive KV pre-seeding and applied per-request max_tokens=512 to reduce tail latency.
- Deployed temporary rate-shaping for the account to limit queue storms.
- Authorized an emergency burst of 8 GPUs (Dedicated pool) for 2 hours; backlog cleared and average P95 improved within ~40m.

Customer impact:
- Reported checkout failures have fallen dramatically; conversion recovered toward baseline during the afternoon. We will continue to monitor for next 24 hours.

Next steps and timeline:
- We will complete a technical postmortem by EOD tomorrow (timeline and root cause analysis).
- Redwood will surface a recommended configuration change to prevent recurrences (routing pin, model pinning, and KV cache seeding).
- We will evaluate appropriate SLA credits and a billing reconciliation for the emergency burst (Sofia will follow up).

Apologies for the disruption. We will keep you updated and share the postmortem. If you'd like a dedicated sync to walk through the technical changes, happy to schedule.

— Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147
